record.original_question: Does there exist a constant c >= 0 such that every non-complete graph G of order n with minimum degree delta(G) >= n/2 + c has rainbow connection number rc(G) = 2? In particular, does the weaker threshold delta(G) >= n/2 already imply rc(G) = 2?

evidence.quote: The minimum number of colors required so that the colored graph is rainbow connected, is called the rainbow connection number, and it is denoted by rc(G).
Problem 4.1 Does there exist a constant c >= 0 such that if G is a non-complete graph of order n with delta(G) >= n/2 + c, then rc(G) = 2? In particular, does delta(G) >= n/2 imply that rc(G) = 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite, simple, connected graph. An edge-coloring of G (not necessarily proper) is called rainbow connected if for every pair of distinct vertices u, v of G there exists a u-v path all of whose edges receive pairwise distinct colors. The rainbow connection number rc(G) is the minimum number of colors in a rainbow connected edge-coloring of G. For a graph G of order n, let δ(G) denote the minimum degree.

(a) Does there exist an absolute constant c ≥ 0 such that every non-complete graph G of order n with δ(G) ≥ n/2 + c satisfies rc(G) = 2?

(b) In particular, does δ(G) ≥ n/2 already imply that rc(G) = 2 for every non-complete graph G of order n?
artifact.status_search_result: The best known result, due to Caro, Lev, Roditty, Tuza, and Yuster, is that δ(G) ≥ n/2 + log n implies rc(G) = 2 for non-complete graphs, with subsequent refinements involving lower-order logarithmic terms. Removing the logarithmic gap—i.e., obtaining a constant c (or c = 0) such that δ(G) ≥ n/2 + c forces rc(G) = 2—appears to remain unresolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: On Rainbow Connection (Caro, Lev, Roditty, Tuza, Yuster)
status_evidence.snippet: If G is a connected graph with n vertices and minimum degree δ ≥ n/2 + log n, then rc(G) ≤ 2.
status_evidence.claim: Best known sufficient condition has an additive log n term, not a constant.

status_evidence.title: An updated survey on rainbow connections of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing minimum-degree thresholds for rc(G)=2 with logarithmic correction terms; the question of replacing log n by a constant remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The constant-gap version of the threshold is still open.

status_evidence.title: Graphs with rainbow connection number two
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of graphs with rc(G)=2; minimum degree thresholds discussed.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizing rc(G)=2 via minimum degree near n/2 is an active question.
